research.job_description_summary: Accenture India hires fresh graduates as Associate Software Engineer (ASE) and, in a higher-paid track, Advanced Associate Software Engineer (AASE). A 2026 candidate account and secondary guides describe a gamified cognitive and behavioral assessment, a technical MCQ test (DSA, DBMS, cloud, networks, MS Office, pseudocode), a coding test, an AI-assisted communication assessment (spoken and written) and a combined technical and HR interview. The official entry-level page was not fetched for exact stage details.
limitations: The official Accenture entry-level pages were located but not fetched, so no round is marked DOCUMENTED; all rounds are REPORTED from a 2026 LeetCode Discuss account (single candidate, AASE) and two 2026 guides.
The LeetCode account does not show a publication date in the extracted text, so its date is blank; the title and content place it in the 2025-26 hiring cycle.
The candidate account is from one AASE candidate. ASE content is therefore mostly original practice aligned to the same stages.

JobRise (2026-02-11) lists about 20 technical questions without attributing them to individuals; those are used only as topic context. Its few attributed anecdotes (a basic HTTP status code question) are single reports.
Freshershunt (2026-08-19) gives no per-question counts; times_reported is recorded as 1 where a question is reported at all.
Package figures (ASE about 4.5 LPA, AASE about 6.5 LPA) differ between sources and were not used in the questions.
The gamified cognitive games cannot be reproduced as text; the R1 items are conventional aptitude proxies.
Spoken-response prompts are original practice prompts; the actual AI-evaluated prompts are not published.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.

questions.prompt: In a certain code, CLOUD is written as DNRYI. How is SKY written in that code?
questions.relevance_to_role: Accounts describe a gamified cognitive and behavioral assessment as the first stage; this item is a conventional aptitude-style proxy.
questions.expected_answer: TMB
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial source that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://freshershunt.in/?p=54935.

mcq.explanation: The shifts are +1, +2, +3, +4, +5 by position (C to D, L to N, O to R, U to Y, D to I). For SKY: S+1 = T, K+2 = M, Y+3 = B, giving TMB.

questions.prompt: A can finish a task in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, how many days do they need?
questions.relevance_to_role: Accounts describe a gamified cognitive and behavioral assessment as the first stage; this item is a conventional aptitude-style proxy.
follow_ups: If A leaves after 3 days, how long does B need?
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial source that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://freshershunt.in/?p=54935.

mcq.explanation: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 per day, so the time is 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of searching for a key in a balanced binary search tree with n nodes?
questions.relevance_to_role: A 2026 candidate account describes a technical MCQ stage (DSA, DBMS, cloud, networks, MS Office, pseudocode).
questions.expected_answer: O(log n)
follow_ups: What if the tree is skewed?
questions.notes: The topic is reported for this stage in candidate or editorial accounts; this item is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://leetcode.com/discuss/post/8381531/accenture-interview-experience-2026-fres-wj1a/.

mcq.explanation: A balanced BST has height O(log n), so a search takes O(log n). An unbalanced tree can degrade to O(n).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a necessary condition for deadlock?
questions.relevance_to_role: A 2026 candidate account describes a technical MCQ stage (DSA, DBMS, cloud, networks, MS Office, pseudocode).
questions.expected_answer: Preemption
follow_ups: How do you prevent circular wait?
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial source that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://jobrise.io/en/blog/accenture-interview-questions-freshers-2026/.

mcq.explanation: The four conditions are mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait. Preemption being allowed prevents deadlock.

questions.prompt: Print all leader elements of an array: elements that are strictly greater than every element to their right.
questions.relevance_to_role: A 2026 candidate account lists a leader-element array problem in the coding stage.
questions.expected_answer: Scan from the right; an element is a leader if it exceeds the maximum seen so far; reverse the collected list.
follow_ups: What changes if 'greater or equal' is used?
questions.notes: Topic reported by one candidate; the problem statement is paraphrased and original in wording.

coding.problem_statement: Given n integers, print all leaders in their original left-to-right order. The last element is always a leader.
coding.expected_algorithm: Scan right to left tracking the running maximum.

questions.prompt: You are given an HTML page with a plain list of cards. Using only CSS, lay the cards out in a responsive three-column grid with equal gaps, and highlight a card on hover.
questions.relevance_to_role: A 2026 candidate account lists a task of modifying a web UI with HTML/CSS in the coding stage.
questions.expected_answer: Use a container with display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 16px; add a media query to reduce columns on small screens; style .card:hover with a box-shadow or background change. Flexbox with wrap is an alternative.
follow_ups: How would you make it two columns on tablets?
questions.notes: Task type reported by one candidate; the specific brief is an original example.

questions.prompt: Tables: Students(id, name), Courses(id, title), Enrollments(student_id, course_id, grade). Write a query listing each student's name, the course title and grade for all enrollments.
questions.relevance_to_role: A 2026 candidate account lists a SQL query joining three tables in the coding stage.
questions.expected_answer: SELECT s.name, c.title, e.grade FROM Enrollments e JOIN Students s ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN Courses c ON c.id = e.course_id; Use LEFT JOIN from Students if students with no enrollment must also appear.
questions.notes: Task type reported by one candidate; the schema is an original example.

Delivery will be late because the team failed.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between an abstract class and an interface? When would you pick each?
questions.relevance_to_role: Accounts describe a roughly 30-minute interview mixing introduction, projects, technical basics and HR questions.
questions.expected_answer: An abstract class can hold state and partial implementation and supports single inheritance; an interface defines a contract (and default methods in modern languages) and a class can implement several. Use abstract classes for shared base behaviour, interfaces for capabilities.
follow_ups: Can an interface have a constructor?
common_mistakes: Saying interfaces can hold instance state

questions.prompt: Explain the ACID properties with a bank-transfer example.
questions.relevance_to_role: Accounts describe a roughly 30-minute interview mixing introduction, projects, technical basics and HR questions.
questions.expected_answer: Atomicity: both debit and credit happen or neither. Consistency: totals remain valid. Isolation: concurrent transfers do not interfere. Durability: committed changes survive failures.
